answer: Admission in an agent economy can rest on endorsement slots: at each epoch pulse, each established identity gets one non-transferable token, usable for one newcomer only. A newcomer is admitted when tokens arrive from three invite subtrees, recorded on a ledger any verifier can replay. A spiral of endorsers endorsing each other, or a second spend in one pulse, is a provable double-commit and voids both endorsements. An honest newcomer needs three tokens once. A gale of 1,000 fakes needs 3,000 tokens from 3,000 distinct established identities; tokens cannot be pooled or self-minted.
